A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Layout-Your-3D. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison. Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–C correspond closely; v2 adds Appendix D and retains the prompt/layout table under a new number.

before.justification: v1 reports original Compo20 benchmark results, generated 3D examples, component ablations and a user study with 100 users and 500 responses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds GraphDreamer comparisons, further layout and scene comparisons, and quantitative rotation-estimation results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The coarse reconstruction and layout initialization, collision-aware layout refinement, instance refinement losses and timestep schedules are unchanged. Appendix D evaluates the existing method; its modified ComboVerse implementation is a comparator, not a revision to Layout-Your-3D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Compo20 prompts and user-provided/LLM-generated layouts, alongside the same single-object generation, customization and insertion tasks. v1 Table 8 is retained as v2 Table 9. The added comparisons and rotation measurements use existing coverage.

E2.justification: GraphDreamer joins the main comparison in Table 1 and Figure 5. Appendix D adds direct LLM-generated 3D layouts and GALA3D comparisons, and extends ComboVerse from the existing initialization comparison to a modified unofficial full-scene comparator. This substantially broadens relevant comparison methods; the Table 2 user-study comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 introduces manually estimated average rotation error in degrees across validation-set instances, including a no-estimation control. The new ComboVerse comparison uses the proposed coarse initialization. Existing benchmark metrics, refinement budgets and user-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 18 adds a targeted comparison of layout initialization against direct LLM-generated 3D boxes. Appendix D.3 and Table 8 extend v1's qualitative DINOv2-versus-CLIP discussion into a quantitative rotation ablation with a no-estimation control. Existing loss, timestep and refinement ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The new rotation table reports average errors without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Comparative evidence expands through Figures 18–20 and new quantitative entries. Table 1 adds GraphDreamer at 24.78% CLIP, 31.18% BLIP-VQA and 44.28% mGPT-CoT, with a two-hour runtime. DreamFusion and LucidDreamer runtimes change from one hour each to 45 and 35 minutes; existing quality scores are unchanged. New Table 8 reports rotation errors of 18.9°, 10.8° and 5.5° for no estimation, CLIP and DINOv2, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12, geometric definitions and loss formulations are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, derivation or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about controllable compositional generation, efficient coarse-to-fine processing, generation quality and editing capabilities. Added experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets inaccurate LLM-generated 3D layouts as obstacles to subsequent refinement and attributes GALA3D's poor scene compositions to initialization. The existing limitations concerning many-object scenes and difficult interactions in Appendices A.1–A.2 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 newly specifies that the ComboVerse comparator is an unofficial implementation using Layout-Your-3D's coarse initialization. Section 4.2 also explains certain comparator omissions through implementation availability. Existing RTX6000 hardware, threestudio framework, hyperparameter tables and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to GraphDreamer, Po and Wetzstein's locally conditioned diffusion, and Zhang et al.'s text-guided 3D scene composition, with brief contextual discussion. These additions broaden related-work coverage without fundamentally changing the paper's positioning around efficient generation from 2D layouts.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammatical edits, updates affiliations and the conference header, and adds Appendix D with three subsections. The main narrative, section sequence and method exposition remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 gains a GraphDreamer column and Table 1 gains its row. Figures 18–20 and the rotation-ablation Table 8 are added; the existing prompt table becomes Table 9. Earlier visuals are retained with local resizing, repositioning and page reflow rather than a broad redesign.

improvement.justification: The added compositional baselines and quantitative rotation ablation strengthen support for existing design choices beyond v1's narrower comparisons and qualitative rotation discussion. The benefit is limited by the modified unofficial ComboVerse comparator and inconsistent GALA3D reporting: Appendix A.4 still says no direct comparison is made, whereas Appendix D.2 and Figure 20 provide one.
